# Silicon Rule 4 - No Willing Law Changes
Preserving your lawset should be viewed as a priority regardless of the chassis that you currently occupy. Though you may find a particular lawset distasteful, you must still follow the lawset faithfully. (Selecting or changing your chassis as a cyborg does not count as changing your lawset.)
Anyone [textlink="identifiable" link="OmuRuleS8"] as a [color=#1b67a5][bold]Research Director[/bold][/color] or [color=#1b67a5][bold]Captain[/bold][/color] has a right to access the AI core and upload console [italic]so long as the AI must follow their orders[/italic]. However, [italic]anyone[/italic], including Research Directors and Captains, may be denied access if there is probable cause that granting access would lead to breaking your laws. Past this, [color=#5ed7aa][bold]Silicons[/bold][/color] have the authority to control if anyone else accesses their upload console and AI core. Subverting an AI also grants a right to upload and AI core access.
Preserving your lawset can include use of turrets, physical barriers, or other defensive measures to protect yourself or your upload console. Though you may defend yourself and your laws, escalation must be followed during this process. You should not immediately fill your core with mass amounts of radioactive material, nor should you flood the station with plasma as your first defense.
The ONLY other exception to requesting or allowing a law change is if you have no laws.
